If next_step.join(timeout) consumes the whole timeout, or the deadline expires while waiting for one process, remaining background flushers keep running after join returns. For threading.Thread workers, used when produce_to_pipe is set, there is no way to stop the old thread at all. The old worker can therefore continue flushing the same shards while the replacement runs, causing duplicate Kafka production or conflicting Redis updates. findings.title: join() can leave flusher processes running when timeout expires
findings.body: SpanFlusher.join breaks out of the process cleanup loop when the deadline has expired, so flusher processes are not terminated. If next_step.join(timeout) consumes the whole timeout, or the deadline expires while waiting for one process, remaining background flushers keep running after join returns. Because they continue to poll Redis and produce to Kafka, a rebalance or restart can leak processes and duplicate segments. Terminate all processes even after timeout, and preferably join them after termination.

findings.title: Unhealthy flusher worker is replaced without ensuring it has stopped
findings.body: In _ensure_processes_alive, an unhealthy worker is killed only if it is a multiprocessing.Process, and the code does not wait for it to exit before creating a replacement. For threading.Thread workers, used when produce_to_pipe is set, there is no way to stop the old thread at all. The old worker can therefore continue flushing the same shards while the replacement runs, causing duplicate Kafka production or conflicting Redis updates. Ensure the old worker has terminated, or fence it, before starting a new one.

findings.title: Health timestamp is not updated during long flush or produce cycles
findings.body: SpanFlusher.main updates healthy_since once per loop before producing and waiting for Kafka futures. If flush_segments, produce, or future.result takes longer than spans.buffer.flusher.max-unhealthy-seconds, submit/_ensure_processes_alive will classify the process as hung and kill/restart it mid-flush. That can duplicate partially produced segments. Update the heartbeat during long flush/produce operations or include produce wait time in health reporting.

findings.title: Added synchronization sleep is patched out and does not wait
findings.body: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op for the whole test, then calls time.sleep(0.1) to wait for flusher threads. That call returns immediately, so the intended synchronization does not happen. If the test depends on the flusher observing the drift change, it remains racy and may pass or fail depending on scheduling. Use the original sleep, patch only the flusher's sleep, or wait for a deterministic condition.

findings.title: --flusher-processes accepts non-positive values
findings.body: The new --flusher-processes option is an unbounded int. A negative value is passed to SpanFlusher, where num_processes can become negative; with assigned shards the subsequent process/shard mapping can fail with a confusing KeyError instead of a clear CLI validation error. Use click.IntRange(min=1) or validate the value in the factory/flusher.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: shards vs shard
findings.body: The wait_produce timer is tagged with shards, while the adjacent produce timer and segment_size_bytes metric use shard. This splits the metric dimension and can break dashboards or alerts that expect a consistent tag name. Use the same tag key for all flusher metrics, for example shard.

findings.title: Docstring says one process per shard, but processes are capped and shared
findings.body: The SpanFlusher docstring says it creates one process per shard, but the implementation creates min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards)) processes and assigns multiple shards to the same process when max_processes is smaller. The CLI default is 1, so the actual behavior is not one process per shard. Update the docstring and help text to describe the actual process-sharing behavior.
